::: {.hero-lead}
A hands-on tutorial on **PowSyBl** and **Dynawo**, two open-source, industrial-grade tools for power system simulation, and on how they combine in **GridFM-Datakit** to generate steady-state and dynamic datasets, including randomized initial states and randomized dynamic events, for training grid foundation models. No prior experience with PowSyBl or Dynawo is required.
:::

::: {.btn-row}
[Set up your machine](setup.qmd){.primary} [Notebooks on GitHub](https://github.com/gfm6w/tutorial) [Conference page](https://gridfm.org/porto/)
:::

## How the tutorial works

Each part is a Jupyter notebook. Run it cell by cell and fill in the exercises, or read the rendered page on this site, which shows every output. The notebooks live in [`notebooks/`](https://github.com/gfm6w/tutorial/tree/main/notebooks) of the tutorial repository, and the pages here are built from the same sources.

::: {.callout-tip title="No installation? Follow along anyway"}
Every page on this site was executed end to end, so all figures and tables are visible without running anything. The [setup page](setup.qmd) gives three ways to run the notebooks yourself, including a ready-made container.
:::

## Companion talk

This tutorial pairs with the conference talk **Enabling Time-Domain Foundation Models with PowSyBl and Dynawo**, which presents the integration of both tools into the Open GridFM DataKit and its role for time-domain grid foundation models.
